job.title: Finance Team Lead
job.description:
ABOUT OUR CLIENT & THE ROLE

Our client is a rapidly growing technology business operating within the healthcare sector. Following changes across the finance leadership team, they are creating a broader Finance Team Lead position to sit directly underneath the Head of Finance and lead the financial operations and reporting function. You will lead a team of four across financial accounting, revenue, AP and AR, while working closely with an established FP&A function.

The opportunity will suit someone who likes getting into the detail, working out what isn't working and actually fixing it. You'll have significant exposure to senior leadership and the opportunity to build a finance function capable of supporting the next stage of the business's growth.

RESPONSIBILITIES
  • Take ownership of the day-to-day financial operations and reporting function.
  • Lead, coach and develop a team across financial accounting, revenue, Accounts Payable and Accounts Receivable.
  • Oversee month-end reporting, reconciliations and the integrity of financial information.
  • Review existing finance processes, identify weaknesses and implement practical improvements.
  • Strengthen controls, reporting and processes as transaction volumes increase with business growth.
  • Work closely with the Head of Finance to continue improving the capability and structure of the finance function.
  • Drive process improvement and automation rather than accepting inefficient legacy processes.
  • Maintain oversight across revenue accounting, debtors, creditors and broader financial operations.
  • Work closely with the FP&A team and wider business to ensure accurate and useful financial information.
  • Build capability and accountability across the team while remaining prepared to get into the detail yourself.
  • Work directly with senior leadership on financial and operational matters as required.
SKILLS & EXPERIENCE
  • Strong technical accounting background with experience across financial reporting and financial operations.
  • Commercial/industry finance experience, ideally within a growing or changing organisation.
  • Previous experience leading, coaching or developing accounting staff.
  • Genuine examples of identifying finance problems, developing solutions and implementing the change yourself.
  • Experience improving processes, controls, reporting or systems within a finance function.
  • Exposure to finance transformation or a well-developed finance environment that has given you a clear understanding of what good looks like.
  • Comfortable remaining hands-on while taking broader ownership of a finance function.
  • Able to operate independently and make decisions without needing constant escalation.
  • Strong stakeholder management skills and confidence dealing directly with senior executives.
  • Able to prioritise effectively in a fast-moving environment with significant competing demands.

job.title: Financial Controller
job.description:
About Our Client

Our client is an established product based business operating across Australia and international markets. With a combination of manufacturing, supply chain and commercial operations, the organisation operates within a dynamic and increasingly complex environment.

The business is entering an important period of growth and transformation, with a focus on strengthening financial capability, improving systems and reporting, and creating greater visibility across commercial and operational performance.

Role Summary

Reporting to the CFO, the Financial Controller will take a broad leadership role across financial control, reporting, commercial finance and business improvement.
This is not a traditional business as usual Financial Controller position. The successful candidate will be responsible for strengthening the financial foundations of the organisation while partnering closely with operational and commercial stakeholders to improve business performance.
A key focus will be improving reporting quality, strengthening controls and developing greater visibility across product profitability, inventory, costing and margins. The role will also play an important part in improving finance systems and processes across an internationally operating business.

Key Responsibilities
  • Lead month end close, financial reporting and general ledger integrity
  • Strengthen financial controls, reporting processes and governance frameworks
  • Develop greater visibility across product profitability, gross margins and operational performance
  • Partner with operational and commercial stakeholders to support business decision making
  • Support inventory management, product costing and supply chain finance
  • Lead budgeting, forecasting and FP&A activities
  • Drive improvements across finance systems, processes and workflow automation
  • Support statutory reporting, audit and compliance requirements
  • Partner closely with the CFO on finance transformation and broader business improvement initiatives
Skills/Experience
  • CA or CPA qualified with strong Financial Controller or Senior Finance Manager experience
  • Experience within manufacturing, FMCG, industrial, wholesale, distribution or another product based environment
  • Strong understanding of inventory, product costing and supply chain finance
  • Demonstrated FP&A and commercial finance capability
  • Strong financial reporting, controls and technical accounting experience
  • Experience improving or optimising ERP systems and finance processes
  • Comfortable working across international operations and with offshore stakeholders
  • Hands on leadership style with the willingness to get into the detail
  • Strong communication skills with the ability to partner effectively across finance and non finance functions
  • Mandarin language capability will be highly regarded given the organisation's international operations, however is not essential
What's In It For You?
  • Broad Financial Controller role with genuine commercial and operational exposure
  • Work directly with the CFO and senior leadership team
  • Exposure to international manufacturing and supply chain operations
  • Opportunity to lead meaningful finance systems and process improvement
  • Genuine scope to influence reporting, commercial insights and business performance
  • $160,000 + Superannuation + STI + LTI

job.title: Finance Business Partner
job.description:
ABOUT OUR CLIENT 

Our client is a large and established organisation operating within a complex, high-volume environment seeking an experienced Finance Business Partner to support a key commercial channel.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Reporting to the Commercial Manager, you will work closely with sales, marketing and category stakeholders to provide accurate analysis and practical commercial advice. The role has ownership across customer and product profitability, commercial investment, forecasting, performance reporting and decision support.

This is a hands-on business partnering position for someone who can get underneath the numbers, challenge assumptions and explain where the business can improve performance. You will need to balance commercial thinking with strong financial control and attention to detail.

RESPONSIBILITIES
  • Partner with sales, marketing and category stakeholders across a key commercial channel.
  • Analyse sales and profitability by customer, channel and product.
  • Provide commercial advice across pricing, promotions, customer investment and product decisions.
  • Manage and analyse commercial spend, including accruals, claims, reconciliations and material movements.
  • Support the financial assessment of new products and other commercial initiatives.
  • Own key elements of the budget and forecasting process across gross margin, marketing investment and operating expenditure.
  • Investigate monthly results and prepare clear commentary on performance, risks and opportunities.
  • Review month-end journals and balance sheet reconciliations across relevant commercial accounts.
  • Deliver accurate daily, weekly and monthly performance reporting.
  • Develop financial models and complete ad hoc analysis to support decision-making.
  • Identify opportunities to improve reporting, processes, controls and commercial outcomes.
  • Take ownership of projects and issues through to resolution.
SKILLS & EXPERIENCE
  • Degree qualified in accounting, commerce, business or a related discipline.
  • CA or CPA qualification.
  • Strong finance business partnering experience within FMCG, consumer goods or another high-volume environment.
  • Experience supporting major retail customers or a similarly complex commercial channel will be highly regarded.
  • Experience managing commercial investment, customer rebates, promotional spend or similar arrangements.
  • Strong understanding of customer, channel, product, price and volume mix.
  • Experience working with large data sets and tracing information across financial systems.
  • Advanced Excel and financial modelling capability.
  • Evidence of using analysis to challenge decisions and improve commercial performance.
  • Strong stakeholder management skills with the confidence to constructively challenge non-finance leaders.
  • Inquisitive, proactive and comfortable working through detailed issues independently.
  • Able to manage a high volume of work without accuracy slipping.

job.title: Accounts Operations Manager
job.description:
ABOUT OUR CLIENT & THE ROLE
Our client is a growing global healthcare technology business operating across Australia, the US, UK and Asia. With continued international growth and an increasingly complex finance environment, they are looking for an experienced Accounts Operations Manager to take ownership of their transactional finance function.

Reporting to the Group Finance Manager, you will lead a team of six across Accounts Payable and Accounts Receivable. The role owns the full procure-to-pay and order-to-cash cycles, alongside cash management and supporting the broader finance team across reconciliations and month-end.

RESPONSIBILITIES
  • Lead and develop the AP and AR teams across multiple locations, setting clear expectations, KPIs and processes.
  • Own the end-to-end AR process including invoicing, collections, cash allocation, ageing, credit control and management of overdue accounts.
  • Own the end-to-end AP process including invoice processing, approval workflows, supplier reconciliations, payments and supplier onboarding.
  • Manage daily cash positions, bank reconciliations and short-term cash flow forecasting.
  • Ensure AP and AR sub-ledgers reconcile accurately to the General Ledger and support month-end close.
  • Establish and improve SOPs, controls, SLAs and reporting across transactional finance.
  • Identify inefficiencies across AP and AR and drive practical process improvements and automation.
  • Partner with Finance, Sales, Procurement, Operations and IT to resolve issues and improve workflows.
  • Support finance transformation, ERP enhancements, UAT and implementation of new processes and systems.
  • Provide management with visibility across ageing, DSO, DPO, cash flow and operational performance.
SKILLS & EXPERIENCE
  • Strong hands-on understanding of both end-to-end Accounts Payable and Accounts Receivable processes.
  • 7+ years' experience within finance operations, including at least 2–3 years managing both AP and AR functions.
  • Demonstrated experience leading and developing transactional finance teams.
  • Able to clearly demonstrate how you have improved an AP or AR function rather than simply overseeing day-to-day processing.
  • Strong understanding of how AP and AR interact with cash management, reconciliations, month-end and the General Ledger.
  • Experience establishing KPIs, controls, procedures and accountability within an accounts team.
  • Experience within a multi-entity or multinational environment will be highly regarded.
  • Exposure to ERP implementations, automation or finance transformation projects would be advantageous.
  • Strong Excel and ERP systems capability.
  • Degree qualification in Accounting, Finance, Business or a related discipline.

job.title: Senior Finance Manager
job.description:
ABOUT OUR CLIENT 

Our client is a large and established organisation operating within a complex, high-volume environment. Following recent changes across its finance function, they are creating a new Senior Finance Manager position to strengthen leadership across corporate finance and finance operations.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Reporting to the Financial Controller, this is a broad role spanning financial reporting, planning, control, compliance, working capital and operational finance. You will combine strategic oversight with hands-on delivery, supported by a capable team including the Finance Operations Manager, while maintaining a strong focus on accuracy and delivery.
The role will suit someone who enjoys improving how a finance function operates, developing people and bringing structure to an environment that has recently undergone significant systems and process change.

RESPONSIBILITIES
  • Lead monthly management reporting, KPI reporting and wider finance submissions.
  • Coordinate the annual budget, rolling forecasts and longer-term financial planning.
  • Oversee month-end and year-end close, including accounting reviews and issue resolution.
  • Maintain balance sheet integrity through strong reconciliations, journal controls and appropriate accounting treatments.
  • Manage statutory reporting, audit, tax compliance and internal control requirements.
  • Oversee cash flow, working capital, treasury, insurance and payment controls.
  • Provide leadership across accounts payable, accounts receivable, pricing, claims and broader finance operations.
  • Monitor operational finance performance and address service, control and resourcing issues.
  • Drive improvements across finance processes, systems, reporting, automation and data quality.
  • Partner with senior stakeholders on business cases, investment decisions and broader projects.
  • Coach and develop finance leaders while building accountability across the wider team.
SKILLS & EXPERIENCE
  • CA, CPA or equivalent professional qualification.
  • At least 10 years’ experience across financial accounting, financial control, planning or finance operations.
  • Previous senior leadership experience across a sizeable and multi-stream finance function.
  • Strong technical accounting knowledge, including Australian reporting, tax, compliance and audit requirements.
  • Experience within FMCG, consumer goods, manufacturing, retail, distribution or another complex, high-volume environment will be highly regarded.
  • Strong ERP, reporting and advanced Excel capability.
  • Evidence of improving processes, controls and team performance during periods of change.
  • Comfortable working at pace and being challenged on the detail.
  • A hands-on leadership style with the ability to develop experienced team members.
  • High standards of accuracy, follow-through and accountability.

job.title: Systems Engineer - Verification & Validation
job.description:
ABOUT OUR CLIENT

Our client is an innovative Melbourne-based technology business developing complex physical products combining mechanical, electrical, control and automation systems. The business is moving through an important stage of commercialisation, with its technology now being deployed into real-world environments.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We are seeking an experienced Systems Engineer to take ownership across Systems Engineering and Verification & Validation. You'll work across the complete product, understanding how its different systems interact and translating field, customer and market feedback into practical engineering and manufacturing improvements.

You'll also lead the end-to-end V&V process as activity ramps up, from requirements and risk-based test planning through to physical testing, troubleshooting and field trials. This is a hands-on engineering role, not a purely documentation-focused V&V position.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
  • Lead Systems Engineering across mechanical, electrical and control systems.
  • Translate field and market feedback into product and manufacturing improvements.
  • Lead end-to-end Verification & Validation activities.
  • Develop and execute test plans, protocols and technical reports.
  • Conduct structured Root Cause Analysis and drive corrective actions.
  • Work closely with software, embedded and broader engineering teams.
  • Support field trials, commissioning and troubleshooting.

  • 5+ years' Systems Engineering and/or V&V experience.

To apply for the role click apply and submit your application.

job.title: P&C Business Partner
job.description:
ABOUT OUR CLIENT

Our client is a well-established Australian business with a significant national footprint and a large, diverse workforce operating across an extensive branch network. Due to continued growth, an opportunity has arisen for an experienced People & Culture Business Partner to join their expanding People & Culture team.

This is a broad, hands-on HR role offering exposure across employee relations, performance management, recruitment, onboarding, HR projects, workforce reporting and generalist HR advisory.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Reporting to the People & Culture Manager, you will partner closely with regional and branch managers to provide practical, commercially focused HR advice across the full employee lifecycle. Working within a lean P&C team, you will have genuine ownership of your portfolio and manage matters from initial advice through to documentation and resolution.

A key focus will be employee relations and performance management, including supporting managers through difficult conversations, misconduct, grievances and investigations. You will also play an active role in recruitment and onboarding, HR reporting, Award interpretation, HRIS administration and process improvement.

This role will suit an emerging HR Business Partner who enjoys working in a fast-paced, operational environment and wants the opportunity to influence managers while remaining hands-on with day-to-day HR.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
  • Partner with regional and branch managers across a multi-site workforce
  • Provide advice across employee relations, performance management and workplace matters
  • Manage misconduct, grievances, investigations and performance processes
  • Coach managers through difficult conversations and people decisions
  • Provide advice on Modern Awards, NES, Fair Work and employment legislation
  • Support end-to-end recruitment, onboarding, probation and offboarding
  • Prepare employment contracts, letters and employee correspondence
  • Support remuneration reviews and Award compliance
  • Produce HR reporting across turnover, absenteeism, engagement and workforce metrics
  • Support HRIS administration, data integrity and reporting
  • Identify and implement improvements across recruitment, onboarding and P&C processes
  • Contribute to employee engagement, learning and broader HR projects
SKILLS & EXPERIENCE 
  • Previous experience as an HR Business Partner, People & Culture Business Partner or experienced HR Advisor
  • Experience supporting a blue-collar, operational, retail, logistics, distribution or similarly frontline workforce
  • Strong practical employee relations and performance management experience
  • Sound knowledge of Modern Awards, National Employment Standards and Fair Work legislation
  • Confidence partnering with and influencing operational managers
  • The ability to communicate effectively with both frontline employees and senior stakeholders
  • Strong written skills and confidence preparing HR documentation and correspondence
  • Strong Microsoft Office skills, particularly Excel and PowerPoint
  • Experience working with HRIS/HR information systems
  • A proactive, solutions-focused approach with strong attention to detail
  • The confidence to challenge constructively and provide clear, practical advice
  • A tertiary qualification in Human Resources, Business or a related discipline will be highly regarded.

job.title: Finance Manager

WHAT IS IN IT FOR YOU?
  • Broad Finance Manager role with genuine influence across the business
  • Direct access to the Managing Director and leadership team
  • Opportunity to shape reporting, processes and commercial decision-making

job.title: Head of Finance - Property
job.description:

job.title: Head of Finance
job.description:
ABOUT OUR CLIENT

Our client is a high-growth, founder-led food and grocery business with a purpose-led model focused on delivering quality products, convenience and value to Australian consumers.
Operating across ecommerce, fresh food and direct-to-consumer delivery, the business has built a strong customer proposition and is continuing to expand its product range and operational footprint. With growth comes increasing complexity, creating an opportunity for an experienced Head of Finance to strengthen the financial foundations of the business and support its next phase of scale.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Reporting into senior leadership, the Head of Finance will take ownership of the finance function and play a key role in driving financial discipline, commercial visibility and sustainable growth across the business.

This is a hands-on leadership position for someone who enjoys building, fixing and improving. You will strengthen reporting and forecasting, improve visibility across cash flow, working capital and margins, and develop the systems, processes and controls required to support a scaling organisation.

Importantly, this is not a role that operates from behind a desk. You will
partner closely with operations, procurement, marketing and senior leadership to understand the drivers of performance, solve problems at their source and turn financial information into practical commercial decisions.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
  • Lead the finance function across reporting, budgeting, forecasting, governance and compliance
  • Own cash flow forecasting and drive improvements across working capital, inventory and supplier terms
  • Develop robust margin and profitability analysis across products, delivery and operational costs
  • Build meaningful KPI reporting to improve visibility across commercial and operational performance
  • Partner with operations, procurement and marketing to improve costs, margins and customer economics
  • Improve finance systems, processes, controls and automation to support future growth
  • Lead monthly reporting and provide clear commercial insights to senior leadership and key stakeholders
  • Evaluate new products, categories, partnerships and growth opportunities through financial modelling and analysis
SKILLS & EXPERIENCE
  • Proven finance leadership experience within a high-growth and operationally complex environment
  • Strong capability across cash flow management, working capital, forecasting and financial modelling
  • Experience within FMCG, food, ecommerce, logistics, subscription or other product and fulfilment-based businesses will be highly regarded
  • Demonstrated experience improving financial reporting, systems, processes and controls
  • Strong commercial acumen with the ability to understand margin and operational cost drivers
  • Proven ability to partner with and influence non-finance stakeholders
  • Hands-on, practical and comfortable moving between strategy and operational detail
  • Strong communication skills with the ability to translate financial information into clear commercial insights
WHAT'S IN IT FOR YOU?
  • Genuine opportunity to own and shape the finance function of a growing consumer business
  • Broad Head of Finance role with significant commercial and operational exposure
  • Work closely with senior leadership and influence key business decisions
  • Opportunity to build scalable systems, processes and finance capability
  • Purpose-led business operating within an exciting and fast-moving consumer market

job.title: Lifecycle Marketing Lead
job.description:
ABOUT OUR CLIENT

Our client is a growing Australian consumer business operating within a dynamic and evolving market. With a strong digital presence and an established customer base, the business is entering its next phase of growth and continuing to invest in its marketing capability. This is an opportunity to join a purpose-led organisation where customer engagement, retention and experience are central to its ongoing success.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Our client is seeking an experienced Lifecycle Marketing Lead to take ownership of the end-to-end lifecycle marketing strategy across its growing subscriber base. Reporting to the Growth Marketing Manager, you will lead the planning, execution and optimisation of email and SMS activity, with a strong focus on customer engagement, retention, reactivation and lifetime value.

This is a hands-on role where you will combine strategic thinking with campaign execution, building sophisticated customer journeys, developing highly targeted segmentation and using data to continually improve performance. 

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
  • Own the end-to-end planning, execution and optimisation of lifecycle marketing campaigns across email and SMS.
  • Develop sophisticated automated customer journeys and workflows designed to improve acquisition, engagement, category adoption and retention.
  • Drive customer acquisition and reactivation initiatives across a substantial existing database.
  • Develop and manage customer segmentation strategies using behavioural and performance data.
  • Analyse campaign performance and customer insights to continually optimise activity against key commercial metrics.
  • Write, test and refine compelling email copy, including subject lines and campaign messaging.
  • Partner with Brand, Design, Performance Marketing, Product, Technology and CX teams to deliver integrated customer experiences.
  • Identify emerging lifecycle marketing trends, technologies and opportunities to continually improve performance.
SKILLS & EXPERIENCE
  • Proven experience managing end-to-end email and lifecycle marketing campaigns.
  • Strong experience building complex automated email workflows and customer journeys.
  • Strong technical capability across email marketing platforms and eCommerce environments.
  • Demonstrated ability to use customer data and segmentation to improve campaign performance.
  • Excellent copywriting skills with a strong understanding of conversion-focused messaging.
  • Experience with Klaviyo will be highly regarded.
  • Experience within subscription, loyalty or retention-focused business models is highly desirable.
  • Exposure to lifecycle communications across email, SMS, push notifications and other digital channels.
  • Strong analytical capability and a commercial approach to measuring marketing performance.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively across Brand, Design, Performance Marketing, Technology and Customer Experience teams.

job.title: Full Stack Developer
job.description:
ABOUT OUR CLIENT

A global leader in public transportation technology is seeking a talented and motivated Senior Software Engineer to join its growing engineering team. Operating in the public transit solutions industry, this organisation has decades of experience delivering innovative, modular systems that improve accessibility and connectivity across cities worldwide. With a strong international footprint across APAC, Europe, and North America, the company fosters a flexible, collaborative, and people-focused culture.

ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Senior Software Engineer, you will work on cutting-edge, mission-critical software that powers modern public transportation systems. You will collaborate closely with platform specialists, hardware experts, and cross-functional teams to design and deliver robust, scalable, and secure solutions that make a real-world impact.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
  • Design, develop, test, and maintain secure, scalable, and reusable software solutions aligned with customer and business needs.
  • Actively contribute to Agile development practices, including sprint planning, reviews, and retrospectives.
  • Collaborate with the Team Lead and Principal Engineer on system design, technical direction, and delivery planning.
  • Mentor and support junior engineers through code reviews, technical guidance, and knowledge sharing.
  • Investigate, troubleshoot, and resolve production incidents to ensure system reliability and customer satisfaction.
  • Communicate technical concepts clearly across multidisciplinary teams, providing constructive and solution-focused feedback.
ESSENTIAL TECHNICAL SKILLS & EXPERIENCE
  • Minimum 5 years of professional software development experience.
  • Strong expertise in Java.
  • Hands-on experience with AWS cloud services, particularly:
    • Serverless architectures (Lambda, API Gateway)
    • Containerisation (ECS, ECR)
    • Infrastructure as Code using CDK
  • Experience using Bitbucket and building CI/CD pipelines for automated testing and deployment.
  • Proven ability to design and integrate RESTful APIs and event-driven architectures (e.g. Kafka).
  • Experience working with relational and non-relational databases, such as Oracle and PostgreSQL.
  • Strong commitment to automated testing, including unit, integration, and UI testing, using tools such as:
    • JUnit, Jest, Selenium, Cucumber Studio, Allure
  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Technology, or a related discipline.
